pairs.why: In B the driving wheels sit on the rails and are joined by side rods behind a proper cowcatcher; A's mixed-size wheels and slab-like pilot don't line up with the track.
A's X-frame folding camp chair has armrests and legs that connect believably, while B's back frame and seat bar overhang and don't join the folding legs in a way that could fold or hold weight.
B's saucer has a consistent hull, rim lights and underside; A is a flat disc with lights stuck on its edge, but neither is clearly broken.
A's life ring hangs by a rope from an eye bolt on the post, while B's ring has a reflection floating apart from it in the water, which breaks the scene.
A has four wheels on axles and a proper tongue, while B shows one oversized wheel, a seat outside the cover and a strut-like tongue that props the wagon up.
A's life ring rope runs to the coil on the post and the pilings stand cleanly in the water, while B's ring reflection is detached and misplaced.
B's wide pedestal and stool bases support the board solidly, like the real card; A's thin pillar under a wide top is less stable, but both could stand.
B's locomotive and tender sit consistently on the track from one camera; A shows the smokebox front almost head-on on a body drawn in side profile, and it has no tender.
